change_markers.text: MY24 update: more power, 82 kWh (gross) versions renamed 45/55
Sportback appears in RDW (no 'Q6 SB E-TRON ...' NL car first admitted 2024; 2025: 'Q6 SB E-TRON PERFORMANCE' 208, 'Q6 SB E-TRON' 185)
xDrive40 appears in RDW (39 NL cars first admitted 2024, none in 2023)
Registrations switch to xDrive45 / xDrive60 / M70 names (RDW: 343 of 406 NL cars first admitted 2025; EEA 2025)
Registrations shift from xDrive30 to eDrive20 (RDW: 2023 xDrive30 3654 of 3858 NL cars; 2024 eDrive20 3311 of 4005)
Major facelift (new body panels and interior)
Launch: 24 and 42 kWh, hatchback, cabrio and 3+1
Extended Range battery update (91 kWh usable)
Facelift: 84 kWh, rear wiper, new controls
Czech (Nosovice) production for Europe; 3-phase 11 kW charger
MY21: 11 kW AC, Pivi Pro infotainment
MY21 update: 3-phase 11 kW charger, new screens
RDW names change from 'EQB 250' to 'EQB 250+' (2023: 444 vs 592; 2024: 1667 vs 26)
Cooper E 40.7 kWh, Cooper SE 54.2 kWh
Europe-built (Sunderland) AZE0 update, 6.6 kW charger option
40 kWh, new body; still CHAdeMO, no active battery cooling
Facelift, renamed Corsa Electric, 51 kWh / 115 kW option
Single-motor FWD Standard and Long Range
MY24: single motor switches to RWD, new motors, 82 kWh Long Range, new front
GTS appears in RDW (127 NL cars first admitted 2026)
GTS appears in RDW (125 NL cars first admitted 2022, 1 in 2021)
Turbo GT in OpenEV from model year 2024
Launch: EV40 (40 kWh) and EV60 (60 kWh)
22 kWh, Q210 motor (43 kW AC charging)
R240 motor (longer range, 22 kW AC max)
52 kWh battery, new interior, optional 50 kW CCS
Refresh: heat pump, chrome delete, powered boot; Shanghai-built supply for Europe
Standard Range Plus moves to LFP battery (late 2021)
Trim names change to RWD / Long Range / Performance
Highland facelift: new front/rear, ventilated seats, rear screen, no stalks
Lower-cost Standard trim announced (European availability unverified)
New front end, HEPA filter, Autopilot hardware 2 (late 2016)
'Raven' update: permanent-magnet front motor, adaptive air suspension
Yoke steering, landscape screen, Plaid tri-motor
Minor refresh (new wheels, lighting, suspension tweaks)
RWD (LFP) entry version added in Europe
Juniper facelift: light bars, new interior, rear screen
Juniper Performance and Standard variants (timing per market unverified)
bZ4X Touring appears in RDW (579 NL cars first admitted 2026)
'LR' / 'KR 210 KW' names appear in RDW (2024: 'PRO KR 210 KW' 19, 'PRO LR 210 KW' 15 NL cars; 'GTX LR 250 KW' 70 in 2025)
Facelift: new front, upgraded interior materials, software 3.x
APP550 motor, Pro S 79 kWh; GTX variant
MY24 update: APP550 motor, new infotainment
ID.7 Tourer appears in registrations (RDW: 'ID.7 TOURER PRO' 511 NL cars first admitted 2024, none in 2023)
EX30 Cross Country appears in registrations (RDW: 79 NL cars first admitted 2025; EEA 2025: 552)
MY24: single motor switches to RWD, new motors

explainer.en: Most electric cars so far use a battery of roughly 300 to 550 volts, usually called "400 V". These cars charge at full speed on almost every DC fast charger, old or new, because the charging network was built around them. Their peak charging power is usually limited to roughly 100 to 250 kW by the current the cables and cells can take.
explainer.nl: De meeste elektrische auto's tot nu toe hebben een accu van ongeveer 300 tot 550 volt, meestal "400V" genoemd. Ze laden op vrijwel elke DC-snellader op volle snelheid, oud of nieuw.

explainer.en: An "800 V" car has a battery of roughly 550 to 850 volts. Higher voltage means less current for the same power, so these cars can usually charge faster and hold high power for longer on modern 800 V-capable chargers. The catch for used buyers: on older 400 V-only chargers the car has to convert the voltage up (a "booster") or charges at reduced power, which can be much slower than the headline figure. Check the "400 V charger behaviour" for the car you are looking at.
explainer.nl: Een "800V"-auto heeft een accu van ongeveer 550 tot 850 volt en laadt op moderne 800V-laders meestal sneller. Op oudere 400V-laders moet de auto de spanning omhoog omzetten of laadt hij met minder vermogen, soms veel trager dan het opgegeven maximum.

explainer.en: A small but growing group of cars uses batteries of roughly 850 volts and up, sometimes marketed as "900 V" or "1000 V". The goal is even higher charging power on the newest chargers. Most existing chargers top out around 920 to 1000 volts, so how these cars behave on older or lower-voltage chargers depends heavily on the car's own converter; treat claims with care until real-world tests exist.
explainer.nl: Een kleine maar groeiende groep auto's gebruikt accu's van ongeveer 850 volt en hoger. Hoe ze zich gedragen op oudere laders hangt sterk af van de omvormer in de auto.

pros.en: High energy density: more range per kilo and per litre of battery.
Good performance in the cold compared with LFP.
Widely used, so long-term ageing behaviour is well understood.

cons.en: Ages faster if kept at a high charge level or high temperature for long periods.
Uses nickel and cobalt, which are costlier and have harder supply chains.

care_tips.en: For daily use, charge to around 80-90 % unless the manual says otherwise; charge to 100 % before long trips.
Avoid leaving the car parked for days at 100 % or near 0 %.

explainer.en: NMC is the most common battery type in European electric cars. It packs a lot of energy into a small space, which helps range. The trade-off is that it prefers not to sit full: most makers suggest a daily limit below 100 %. Numbers like NMC622 or NMC811 describe the mix of nickel, manganese and cobalt; more nickel usually means more energy and less cobalt.
explainer.nl: NMC is de meest gebruikte accusoort in Europese elektrische auto's: veel energie in weinig ruimte, maar hij staat liever niet lang volgeladen.

pros.en: High energy density, similar to or above NMC.
Proven over many years in high-mileage cars.

cons.en: Like NMC, ages faster when kept full or hot.

care_tips.en: For daily use, charge to around 80-90 % unless the manual says otherwise.
Charge to 100 % only shortly before a long trip.

explainer.en: NCA is a close relative of NMC, best known from Tesla cars with Panasonic cells. It behaves much like NMC for owners: lots of energy, and it is happiest kept between roughly 20 % and 80-90 % in daily use.
explainer.nl: NCA is familie van NMC, vooral bekend van Tesla's met Panasonic-cellen. Voor de eigenaar gedraagt hij zich vrijwel hetzelfde als NMC.

pros.en: Makers usually allow charging to 100 % every day.
Long cycle life and a good safety record.
No nickel or cobalt, so cheaper to make.

cons.en: Lower energy density: a heavier or bigger pack for the same range.
More range and charging-speed loss in cold weather.
The car's charge-level estimate can drift; it needs a full charge now and then to recalibrate.

care_tips.en: Charge to 100 % regularly (many makers suggest at least weekly) so the car can recalibrate its range estimate.
In winter, precondition the battery before fast charging.

explainer.en: LFP batteries hold less energy per kilo than NMC, but they are robust and cheaper. For owners, the big plus is simple: most makers say you can charge to 100 % every day without worrying. The downside is cold weather, where both range and fast-charging speed drop more than with nickel-based batteries.
explainer.nl: LFP-accu's bevatten minder energie per kilo, maar zijn robuust en goedkoper. Meestal mag je ze elke dag tot 100 % laden; in de kou zakken bereik en laadsnelheid meer.

pros.en: Aims for more energy than LFP while keeping most of its low cost and robustness.

cons.en: Few cars use it yet, so there is little real-world ageing data.
Often blended with other chemistries, which makes its behaviour harder to predict.

care_tips.en: Follow the manual's charging advice; general LFP rules may not apply.

explainer.en: LMFP adds manganese to LFP to raise its voltage and energy content. It is new in cars, and sometimes mixed with NMC, so we do not yet know how it ages over many years. Whether daily 100 % charging is fine depends on the maker; we leave that open until guidance is clear.
explainer.nl: LMFP voegt mangaan toe aan LFP voor meer energie. Het is nieuw in auto's; hoe het op lange termijn veroudert, weten we nog niet goed.

pros.en: Cheap and simple; used in many early electric cars.

cons.en: Ages relatively quickly, especially in hot climates and without active cooling.
Lower energy density than modern NMC.

care_tips.en: Check the state of health (SoH) before buying; capacity loss varies a lot between cars.
Avoid repeated fast charges on hot days, as heat speeds up ageing.

explainer.en: Several early electric cars used a blend of lithium manganese oxide (LMO) with some nickel-based material. These packs were cheap but tend to lose capacity faster, especially in heat. For a used car with this chemistry, the battery's state of health matters more than the age or mileage alone. Exactly which early cars used which blend is not always clearly documented.
explainer.nl: Een aantal vroege elektrische auto's gebruikte een mengsel op basis van mangaanoxide. Die accu's verouderen sneller, vooral bij warmte; check de accugezondheid (SoH).

pros.en: Uses sodium instead of lithium: cheap, abundant materials.
Expected to cope better with cold than LFP.

cons.en: Low energy density so far, so mainly suited to small city cars.
Very few cars on sale; long-term data is missing.

care_tips.en: Follow the manual's charging advice; there are no established rules of thumb yet.

explainer.en: Sodium-ion batteries work like lithium-ion but use sodium, which is cheap and plentiful. They store less energy, so the first cars using them are small and short-range, mostly in China. It is too early to say how they age or what charging habits suit them best.
explainer.nl: Natrium-ion werkt als lithium-ion maar met goedkoop natrium. De eerste auto's zijn klein en hebben weinig bereik; over veroudering is nog weinig bekend.

pros.en: Less liquid electrolyte, aiming for higher energy density and better safety.

cons.en: Only a handful of mostly Chinese cars use it, often as an expensive option.
The term is used loosely in marketing; designs differ a lot.

explainer.en: "Semi-solid" batteries replace part of the liquid inside the cell with a gel or solid material. They are a step towards full solid-state batteries. The name is used loosely, and very few cars have them, so treat range and ageing claims as unproven.
explainer.nl: "Semi-vaste" accu's vervangen een deel van de vloeistof in de cel door gel of vaste stof. Nog maar weinig auto's hebben ze; claims zijn onbewezen.

pros.en: Promises higher energy density, faster charging and better safety than today's cells.

cons.en: As far as we know, not yet in a series-production passenger car; timelines keep moving.

explainer.en: All-solid-state batteries use no liquid electrolyte at all. Many makers have announced them, but to our knowledge none is in a regular production car yet. Until there is one, treat announced figures as targets, not facts.
explainer.nl: Volledig vaste-stofaccu's hebben helemaal geen vloeibaar elektrolyt. Ze zijn veel aangekondigd, maar voor zover wij weten nog niet in een seriemodel te koop.

pros.en: Aims for NMC-like energy with much less cobalt and nickel, using cheaper manganese.

cons.en: Not yet in series cars as far as we know; historically struggled with voltage fade over time.

explainer.en: Lithium manganese-rich (LMR) cells are a research and pre-production chemistry that some large carmakers have said they plan to use later this decade. Earlier versions lost voltage as they aged; whether that is solved will only be clear once cars are on the road.
explainer.nl: LMR is een mangaanrijke accusoort die enkele grote merken later dit decennium willen gebruiken. Of oudere problemen met veroudering zijn opgelost, moet nog blijken.

explainer.en: A coolant loop runs through or under the battery, usually linked to a radiator, a heater and often the heat pump. This is the most common setup today. It keeps the battery at a good temperature while fast charging and driving hard, so charging speeds hold up better and the battery ages more gently.
explainer.nl: Een koelvloeistofcircuit loopt langs de accu. Dat houdt de temperatuur goed bij snelladen, zodat de laadsnelheid beter op peil blijft.

explainer.en: The battery is cooled directly by the car's air-conditioning refrigerant instead of a separate coolant loop. It can cool well, but how well it heats the battery in winter depends on the design. Used by a few makers, for example in the BMW i3.
explainer.nl: De accu wordt direct gekoeld met het koudemiddel van de airco, zonder apart koelvloeistofcircuit. Bijvoorbeeld gebruikt in de BMW i3.

explainer.en: Fans blow air (sometimes cabin air) over the battery. This is cheaper and lighter than liquid cooling but removes heat less effectively, so repeated fast charges or hot weather can slow charging down. Mostly seen in older or smaller cars.
explainer.nl: Ventilatoren blazen lucht langs de accu. Goedkoper, maar minder effectief: bij herhaald snelladen of warm weer kan het laden vertragen.

explainer.en: The battery has no fans or coolant loop and simply sheds heat through its casing. After one or two fast charges on a long trip the battery gets hot and the car limits charging power, sometimes sharply (owners of the early Nissan Leaf call this "rapidgate"). Fine for daily commuting, less so for long road trips.
explainer.nl: De accu heeft geen ventilator of koelcircuit. Na een of twee snellaadbeurten wordt hij warm en laadt de auto trager ("rapidgate").

short.en: The range from the official EU lab test. Real-world range is usually lower, especially in winter and on motorways.
short.nl: Het bereik uit de officiële EU-labtest. In de praktijk meestal lager, vooral in de winter en op de snelweg.

long.en: WLTP is the standard test cycle used in Europe to rate range and consumption. It is useful for comparing cars with each other, but it is run in mild conditions with a mix of slow and fast driving. Most cars get noticeably less in daily use, which is why we also show our own real-world range.

nerd_note.en: WLTP replaced NEDC from 2017-2018; NEDC figures for older cars are far more optimistic and are never mixed with WLTP here.

short.en: How far the car is likely to go in normal driving, from our own data and calculations.
short.nl: Hoe ver de auto waarschijnlijk komt bij normaal rijden, op basis van onze eigen data en berekeningen.

long.en: Our real-world range is an estimate of what an average driver gets on a full battery in mixed driving. It comes from owner data or tests where we have them, and from a fallback calculation where we do not. The figure always shows which method produced it.

nerd_note.en: Computed on usable capacity, not gross. The method used is the real-range rung (see that term).

short.en: Which method produced the real-world range: owner data, a direct test, or an estimate from similar cars.
short.nl: Welke methode het praktijkbereik gaf: eigenaardata, een directe test of een schatting op basis van vergelijkbare auto's.

long.en: We use a ladder of methods for real-world range and take the best one available. The top rung is owner data, then a direct test of this exact variant, then a sibling variant, then a ratio for similar cars by brand, body and drivetrain, and finally a ratio by body type. Lower rungs are less precise, so we show which one was used.

nerd_note.en: Rungs in order: owner-data, exact-test, sibling-variant, brand-body-drivetrain-ratio, body-ratio.

short.en: How much electricity the car uses per 100 km. Lower is better, like litres per 100 km.
short.nl: Hoeveel stroom de auto per 100 km verbruikt. Lager is beter, net als liters per 100 km.

long.en: Consumption tells you how efficient a car is. A small, aerodynamic car may use around 14 kWh per 100 km, a big SUV 20 or more. It drives your running costs and, together with battery size, your range.

nerd_note.en: Stored internally as Wh/km. Lab figures usually include charging losses; trip-computer figures usually do not.

label.nl: Thuis en aan de paal laden

short.en: Slower charging at home or at street posts. The car's onboard charger sets the maximum speed.
short.nl: Langzamer laden thuis of aan een laadpaal. De lader in de auto bepaalt de maximale snelheid.

long.en: AC charging uses the car's built-in charger to turn mains power into battery power. Typical limits are 7.4 kW on one phase or 11 kW on three phases; some cars allow 22 kW. It is what you use overnight or at work, so the car's limit matters more than the post's.

nerd_note.en: Some older cars only charge on one phase (around 3.7 or 7.4 kW), which is slow on 3-phase posts common in the Netherlands.

short.en: Fast charging on the road, bypassing the car's onboard charger. Speed depends on the car and the charger.
short.nl: Snel laden onderweg, buiten de lader in de auto om. De snelheid hangt af van auto en laadpaal.

long.en: DC fast chargers feed power straight into the battery, which allows much higher speeds than AC. How fast a car really charges depends on its charge curve, battery temperature and the charger's own limits. Some older or cheaper cars have no fast-charging socket at all.

nerd_note.en: Plugs: CCS2 is the European standard; older Nissan, Mitsubishi and Kia models used CHAdeMO, which fewer new chargers support.

short.en: How many kilometres of real-world range a fast charger adds in 20 minutes. The most practical charging number.
short.nl: Hoeveel kilometer praktijkbereik een snellader in 20 minuten toevoegt. Het meest praktische laadgetal.

long.en: Peak charging power alone says little about a road trip. This figure combines how fast the battery charges with how efficient the car is, giving the kilometres you get back during a typical coffee stop. It assumes a suitable charger and a warm battery.

nerd_note.en: Derived from the charge curve and real-world consumption; starting state of charge assumed around 10 %.

short.en: How charging power changes as the battery fills. A flat, high curve means quick stops.
short.nl: Hoe het laadvermogen verandert terwijl de accu vol raakt. Een vlakke, hoge curve betekent korte stops.

long.en: No car charges at its peak speed all the way. Power usually drops as the battery fills, and the shape of that drop matters more than the peak. A car that holds 100 kW from 10 % to 70 % can beat one that peaks at 200 kW for a few minutes.

nerd_note.en: Curves depend on battery temperature and software version; we show the source and date of each curve.

short.en: The highest fast-charging power the car reaches, usually only briefly and under ideal conditions.
short.nl: Het hoogste snellaadvermogen dat de auto haalt, meestal maar kort en onder ideale omstandigheden.

long.en: Makers like to advertise peak charging power. It is reached only for a short time, with a warm battery at a low charge level. Look at the 10-80 % time or range added in 20 minutes for a fairer picture.

nerd_note.en: Peak figures are often the maker's claim; measured peaks can differ by software version and charger.

short.en: Minutes to fast charge from 10 % to 80 %. The usual way to compare charging speed.
short.nl: Minuten om snel te laden van 10 % naar 80 %. De gebruikelijke manier om laadsnelheid te vergelijken.

long.en: Charging is fastest in the middle of the battery, so the industry compares cars on the time from 10 % to 80 %. Remember that a bigger battery adds more kilometres in that time, so compare it together with range added in 20 minutes.

nerd_note.en: Assumes a charger stronger than the car's peak and a battery at optimal temperature.

short.en: Whether the car uses a 400 V or 800 V battery. It affects charging speed, especially on older chargers.
short.nl: Of de auto een 400V- of 800V-accu heeft. Dat beïnvloedt de laadsnelheid, vooral op oudere laders.

long.en: Most electric cars run at around 400 volts; a growing number use around 800 volts. Higher voltage allows faster charging on modern chargers, but on older 400 V chargers an 800 V car may be slower. We group cars into classes by the battery's nominal voltage.

nerd_note.en: Class is derived from nominal pack voltage: 400v 300-550 V, 800v 550-850 V, 900v-plus 850-1100 V. Some small '800 V' packs sit near 520 V nominal.

short.en: How fast an 800 V car charges on older 400 V chargers: full speed, via a booster, or limited.
short.nl: Hoe snel een 800V-auto laadt op oudere 400V-laders: volle snelheid, via een booster of beperkt.

long.en: Many fast chargers, especially older ones, can only deliver up to about 500 volts. A 400 V car charges on them normally. An 800 V car needs to convert the voltage up with a booster, or it charges at reduced power; on some cars this is much slower than the advertised peak.

nerd_note.en: Values: native, booster (with kW), limited (with kW), not-disclosed. Figures change with software updates.

short.en: A converter that lets an 800 V car charge on a 400 V charger, often at reduced power.
short.nl: Een omvormer waarmee een 800V-auto aan een 400V-lader kan laden, vaak met minder vermogen.

long.en: An 800 V car cannot take power directly from a charger that only goes up to about 500 volts. Some cars add a separate boost converter; others reuse the electric motor and its inverter to step up the voltage. The booster's own power limit sets the charging speed on those chargers.

nerd_note.en: Hyundai/Kia E-GMP cars reuse the rear motor and inverter as the booster; reported 400 V charging power varies with software.

short.en: The materials inside the battery cells. It affects range, cost, cold weather and how full to charge daily.
short.nl: De materialen in de accucellen. Bepaalt bereik, prijs, gedrag in de kou en hoe vol je dagelijks laadt.

long.en: Most electric cars use a nickel-based chemistry (NMC or NCA) or iron phosphate (LFP). Nickel types hold more energy but prefer not to sit at 100 %; LFP holds less but is usually happy being charged full every day. Newer chemistries such as sodium-ion are only starting to appear.

nerd_note.en: Makers often do not publish the chemistry; we show not-disclosed rather than guess.

short.en: How the car keeps its battery at a good temperature. Matters for fast charging and battery life.
short.nl: Hoe de auto de accu op een goede temperatuur houdt. Belangrijk voor snelladen en levensduur.

long.en: Batteries charge and age best within a comfortable temperature range. Liquid cooling is the most effective and most common; air cooling and no active cooling are cheaper but can slow fast charging on long trips. Good thermal management also helps with winter charging.

nerd_note.en: Types: liquid, refrigerant, air, passive. Heating matters as much as cooling in cold climates.

short.en: Cells are fitted directly into the battery pack without separate modules, saving weight and space.
short.nl: De cellen zitten direct in het accupakket, zonder losse modules. Dat bespaart gewicht en ruimte.

long.en: Traditional packs group cells into modules, then modules into a pack. Cell-to-pack skips the module step, so more of the pack is active battery material. It can make repairs harder, because a fault may not be fixable by swapping one module.

nerd_note.en: BYD Blade and several CATL packs are cell-to-pack. Repairability depends on the specific design.

short.en: The physical shape of the battery cells: flat pouches, hard boxes, round cylinders or long blades.
short.nl: De vorm van de accucellen: platte zakjes, harde blokjes, ronde cilinders of lange 'blades'.

long.en: Battery cells come in a few shapes. Pouch cells are flat and light, prismatic cells are hard rectangular cans, cylindrical cells look like oversized AA batteries, and blade cells are long, thin prismatic cells. For owners the shape matters less than chemistry and cooling.

nerd_note.en: Cylindrical sizes: 18650, 2170 (21700), 4680. Blade is BYD's long prismatic LFP format.

short.en: Usable capacity is what you can actually drive on. Total (gross) includes a hidden reserve.
short.nl: Bruikbare capaciteit is wat je echt kunt gebruiken. Totaal (bruto) bevat een verborgen reserve.

long.en: Makers keep part of the battery in reserve to protect it, so the usable capacity is smaller than the total. Brochures quote either figure, which makes comparisons confusing. We use usable capacity for range calculations and show which one a source quoted.

nerd_note.en: Buffers are typically a few percent up to about 10 %; some makers changed buffers by software update.

short.en: An efficient heater that uses less battery in winter than a simple electric heater, saving range.
short.nl: Een zuinige verwarming die in de winter minder stroom kost dan een gewone elektrische kachel.

long.en: Heating the cabin with a plain resistive heater can use a lot of energy in cold weather. A heat pump moves heat instead of making it, using noticeably less electricity. On many used cars it was an option, so check whether the car you look at has one.

nerd_note.en: Gains are largest around 0-10 °C; in deep frost heat pumps lose efficiency and may fall back on resistive heating.

short.en: The car heats or cools the battery before fast charging so it charges at full speed.
short.nl: De auto verwarmt of koelt de accu vóór het snelladen, zodat hij op volle snelheid laadt.

long.en: A cold battery charges slowly. Many cars warm the battery automatically when you navigate to a fast charger, or let you start it manually. Without it, winter fast charging can take much longer than the brochure suggests.

nerd_note.en: Some older cars added preconditioning only via later software updates; others never got it.

short.en: How much capacity the battery still has compared with new. Key when buying a used electric car.
short.nl: Hoeveel capaciteit de accu nog heeft ten opzichte van nieuw. Belangrijk bij een tweedehands EV.

long.en: All batteries slowly lose capacity with age and use. State of health compares today's capacity with the original, so 90 % means about 10 % less range than new. Ask for a recent battery report; many batteries also have a warranty that guarantees a minimum SoH.

nerd_note.en: SoH is measured differently per maker and tool; treat small differences between reports with care.

short.en: A version of a model that stayed broadly the same over several years, until a major redesign.
short.nl: Een versie van een model die jarenlang grotendeels gelijk bleef, tot een grote vernieuwing.

long.en: We group each model into generations: periods with the same basic design. Facelifts and battery updates inside a generation are shown as change markers. This makes it easier to compare used cars from different years.

nerd_note.en: Hierarchy: make, model, generation, variant. Generation year spans are model years on sale in Europe.

short.en: A specific battery and motor combination within a generation, such as the long-range version.
short.nl: Een specifieke combinatie van accu en motor binnen een generatie, zoals de long range-versie.

long.en: Within one generation, cars come with different batteries, motors and drivetrains. Each of those is a variant, and specs like range and charging speed belong to the variant. Trim levels that only change equipment are not separate variants.

nerd_note.en: A variant points to one platform and one battery pack and inherits the pack's facts unless it has its own.

short.en: The shared technical base under several models, such as Volkswagen's MEB or Hyundai's E-GMP.
short.nl: De gedeelde technische basis onder meerdere modellen, zoals MEB van Volkswagen of E-GMP van Hyundai.

long.en: Carmakers build several models on one shared base of battery, motors and electronics. Cars on the same platform often charge and age in similar ways. Some older electric cars were built on platforms designed for petrol cars.

nerd_note.en: Platform names are partly marketing; we record the owner group and nominal voltage where known.

short.en: The complete battery in the car. Several versions or models often share the same pack.
short.nl: De complete accu in de auto. Meerdere uitvoeringen of modellen delen vaak hetzelfde pakket.

long.en: A battery pack is the full assembly of cells, cooling, electronics and casing. We store pack facts once, such as capacity, chemistry and supplier, and every variant using that pack inherits them. If a variant has its own measured figure, that one wins.

nerd_note.en: Pack facts in the seed data are hand-entered with low confidence until sourced.

short.en: When a hot battery makes the car charge slower after one or two fast charges on a trip.
short.nl: Als een warme accu de auto trager laat laden na een of twee snellaadbeurten onderweg.

long.en: Without active cooling, a battery heats up during fast charging and stays warm. The car then reduces charging power to protect it, so the second or third stop on a long trip takes much longer. The name comes from early Nissan Leaf owners.

nerd_note.en: Most common on cars with passive or air cooling; liquid-cooled packs can still throttle in extreme heat.

short.en: How well checked a figure is: hand-checked by us, confirmed by several sources, or from one source.
short.nl: Hoe goed een gegeven is gecontroleerd: door ons, door meerdere bronnen bevestigd of uit één bron.

long.en: Every number on this site has a quality tier. Checked means a person compared it with a primary source. Sourced means at least two independent sources agree. Single-source means we have only one source so far.

nerd_note.en: Tiers: checked, sourced, single-source. Independent of confidence, which describes the source itself.

short.en: Two or more independent sources give the same value, within a small tolerance.
short.nl: Twee of meer onafhankelijke bronnen geven dezelfde waarde, binnen een kleine marge.

long.en: When different sources report the same figure, we can be more sure it is right. If they disagree, we show the spread and the sources, rather than silently picking one.

nerd_note.en: Tolerance depends on the field, for example a few percent for capacity or range.

short.en: Our judgement of how reliable a value is, based on its source and how it was obtained.
short.nl: Ons oordeel over hoe betrouwbaar een waarde is, op basis van de bron en hoe hij is verkregen.

long.en: Each fact carries a confidence level. High usually means an official or measured value from a reliable source; low means hand-entered or estimated. Low-confidence values are shown but marked, and are replaced as better sources come in.

nerd_note.en: Values: high, medium, low. Nerd mode shows source, retrieval date and confidence for every fact.

short.en: A value we calculated from related data, not measured directly on this exact car.
short.nl: Een waarde die we berekenden uit verwante gegevens, niet direct gemeten aan precies deze auto.

long.en: Where no direct measurement exists, we estimate, for example from a sibling variant or a similar car. Estimates are always labelled and show the method used. They are replaced as soon as a measured value is available.

nerd_note.en: For real-world range, the method is the real-range rung.

short.en: A figure published by the carmaker, not checked by independent tests.
short.nl: Een getal van de fabrikant zelf, niet gecontroleerd door onafhankelijke tests.

long.en: Makers publish figures such as peak charging power or 10-80 % time. These are useful but often measured in ideal conditions. Where we have independent tests, we show them next to the claim.

nerd_note.en: Official homologation values (like WLTP) are regulated tests and treated separately from marketing claims.

short.en: A group of model years with similar technology, used to compare cars of similar age.
short.nl: Een groep modeljaren met vergelijkbare techniek, om auto's van gelijke leeftijd te vergelijken.

long.en: Electric car technology moved quickly, so a 2016 car and a 2024 car are hard to compare directly. We group cars into eras by model year. Within an era, range, charging and prices are more comparable.

nerd_note.en: Eras: pre-2018, 2018-20, 2021-22, 2023-24, 2025+. Pre-2018 cars mostly have only NEDC figures.

short.en: The maker has not published this, and we have no reliable source yet. We do not guess.
short.nl: De fabrikant heeft dit niet gepubliceerd en we hebben nog geen betrouwbare bron. We gokken niet.

long.en: Some technical details, such as cell supplier or exact voltage, are not published for many cars. Rather than fill the gap with a guess, we show that the value is not disclosed. If you have a reliable source, it can be added.

nerd_note.en: 'not-disclosed' is a valid value for every pack, platform and voltage field (Decision 010).

short.en: The battery's typical working voltage. It changes slightly with charge level; the maximum is higher.
short.nl: De gebruikelijke werkspanning van de accu. Die varieert met de laadstand; het maximum ligt hoger.

long.en: A battery's voltage rises as it charges and falls as it empties. The nominal voltage is the typical middle value; the maximum is reached when full. We use the nominal value to place a car in a voltage class.

nerd_note.en: Nominal is roughly cells in series times about 3.6-3.7 V for NMC, about 3.2 V for LFP.

short.en: Price when bought new in this country, if still on sale.
short.nl: Prijs bij aankoop nieuw in dit land, als hij nog te koop is.

long.en: The list price when the car was on sale new in this country, in local currency. Used cars sell for much less; this is a reference, not a market value.

nerd_note.en: Tonight only German euro prices from Open EV Data are available; NL will use the RDW catalogue price later.

short.en: How many of this generation are registered in the Netherlands.
short.nl: Hoeveel van deze generatie in Nederland geregistreerd zijn.

long.en: How many of these cars are registered in the Netherlands, from RDW open data. A high number means more choice on the used market and easier parts and servicing.

nerd_note.en: Counted per generation from RDW first-admission data with a no-engine proxy for battery-electric cars (Q-010). Imports count from their first foreign registration.

technical.en: Model years on sale in Europe

short.en: The years this version was sold new in Europe.
short.nl: De jaren waarin deze versie nieuw te koop was in Europa.

long.en: The years this generation or variant was sold in Europe. Boundaries marked as not yet checked may shift by a year.

nerd_note.en: Year bands come from the hand-made seed list; uncertain ones are flagged in the data, not hidden.

short.en: European size class, from city car (A) to large SUV.
short.nl: Europese grootteklasse, van stadsauto (A) tot grote SUV.

long.en: The European size class, from A (city car) to F (luxury), with J for SUVs. It helps compare cars of similar size and price.

nerd_note.en: Assigned by hand in the seed list; segment borders are a judgement call.

short.en: Hatchback, saloon, estate, SUV and so on.
short.nl: Hatchback, sedan, stationwagen, SUV enzovoort.

long.en: The shape of the car: hatchback, sedan, estate, SUV and so on. It affects boot space, height and real-world range.

nerd_note.en: Body type also drives the provisional real-range ratio when no tests exist.

short.en: Luggage space behind the rear seats.
short.nl: Bagageruimte achter de achterbank.

long.en: Luggage space behind the rear seats in litres, seats up. Makers measure it in different ways, so small differences mean little.

nerd_note.en: VDA litres where known; some makers quote to the roof or include under-floor space, so compare with care.

short.en: Bumper to bumper, handy for parking spaces and garages.
short.nl: Van bumper tot bumper, handig voor parkeerplekken en garages.

long.en: Overall length in millimetres, bumper to bumper. Useful for parking spaces, garages and ferries.

nerd_note.en: From type-approval or maker data; tolerance 10 mm between sources (Decision 009).

short.en: Heaviest braked trailer the car is approved to tow.
short.nl: Zwaarste geremde aanhanger die de auto mag trekken.

long.en: The heaviest braked trailer the car is approved to tow, in kilograms. Zero means it is not approved for towing.

nerd_note.en: Braked figure from type approval where available; towing cuts range sharply.

short.en: Some batteries (mostly LFP) are fine at 100% every day; others prefer about 80%.
short.nl: Sommige accu's (vooral LFP) kunnen elke dag 100%; andere liever ongeveer 80%.

long.en: Whether the battery chemistry is happy being charged to 100% every day. LFP batteries usually are; most others prefer about 80% for daily use.

nerd_note.en: From the chemistry table; always follow the maker's own guidance for the specific car.

short.en: You borrow part of the price and pay it back monthly with interest. The car is yours.
short.nl: Je leent een deel van de prijs en betaalt het maandelijks terug met rente. De auto is van jou.

long.en: With a loan you buy the car, put down a deposit if you like, and repay the rest in fixed monthly amounts over an agreed term. Interest is the price of borrowing, shown as an APR that includes most fees. Our monthly figure is an estimate from a typical national rate, not an offer from a lender.

nerd_note.en: Annuity formula: payment = P × r / (1 − (1 + r)^−n), with n months and monthly rate r = (1 + APR)^(1/12) − 1. Typical rates come from central-bank consumer-credit statistics (finance_profiles), not lender quotes; with no source the calculator asks you for a rate.

short.en: You rent the car for a fixed monthly fee and hand it back at the end. You never own it.
short.nl: Je huurt de auto voor een vast bedrag per maand en levert hem aan het eind weer in.

long.en: A lease is a long-term rental: you pay a fixed amount each month for an agreed term and mileage, and return the car at the end. The leasing company owns the car and carries the loss in value, and often insurance and maintenance too. Extra kilometres or damage at hand-back can cost extra.

nerd_note.en: A lessor prices the lease from expected depreciation (price minus residual value), its funding cost and any services. We show no lease figures until partner feeds exist; lease links are labelled and never change rankings.

short.en: A lease for private people, not companies: one monthly price, usually including insurance, maintenance and road tax.
short.nl: Lease voor particulieren: één maandbedrag, meestal inclusief verzekering, onderhoud en wegenbelasting.

long.en: Private lease is the consumer version of a company-car lease and is common in the Netherlands. You pay one all-in monthly amount and return the car at the end of the term. In the Netherlands it comes with a credit check and a BKR registration, and providers with the Keurmerk Private Lease follow its code of conduct.

nerd_note.en: Used-car ('occasion') private lease exists in NL. The closest French products are LLD (long-term rental) and LOA (rental with an option to buy). Term length and yearly kilometres move the price most.

short.en: Lower monthly payments, then one large final payment: pay it, hand the car back, or trade in.
short.nl: Lagere maandbedragen en aan het eind één grote slottermijn: betalen, auto inleveren of inruilen.

long.en: With balloon finance part of the price is left over as one large payment at the end of the term, so the monthly amounts are lower. In the UK this is called PCP (personal contract purchase), and the French LOA works in a similar way. You pay more interest overall than on a normal loan of the same size, because the balloon stays borrowed for the whole term.

nerd_note.en: The balloon is usually set near the lender's guaranteed future value (GFV) of the car, a form of residual value. Monthly payment = annuity on (amount borrowed − present value of the balloon).

short.en: What the car is expected to be worth at the end of a loan or lease.
short.nl: Wat de auto naar verwachting nog waard is aan het eind van een lening of lease.

long.en: Residual value is the expected price of the car at the end of a contract. It sets the balloon in PCP-style finance and much of the monthly price of a lease, because you mostly pay for the value the car loses. Battery health and the model's used-price trend both affect it.

nerd_note.en: For a lease, the depreciation part of the monthly price is roughly (price − residual value) / months, plus funding cost on the average balance. A residual value is a forecast, not a guarantee, unless the contract guarantees it.

short.en: Everything you pay from start to end: deposit, all monthly payments and any final payment.
short.nl: Alles wat je van begin tot eind betaalt: aanbetaling, alle maandbedragen en een eventuele slottermijn.

long.en: A low monthly amount can hide a high total, so every monthly figure here also shows the total paid over the term. For a loan it is the deposit plus all monthly payments plus any balloon. The difference between this total and the cash price is the cost of borrowing.

nerd_note.en: Under the EU consumer credit directive (CCD2, Directive (EU) 2023/2225), credit adverts that show cost figures must give a representative example that includes the total amount payable. Our calculator is an estimate, not an offer, but shows the same figures.

short.en: The car can give power back, not only take it: to appliances, your home or the grid.
short.nl: De auto kan stroom teruggeven, niet alleen laden: aan apparaten, je huis of het net.

long.en: Two-way charging comes in three levels: powering appliances (V2L), powering your home (V2H) and feeding the grid (V2G). Whether a car can do it depends on the car, its software and battery size, an approved wallbox and, for V2G, an energy contract. The power electronics sit either in the car (AC route, simpler wallbox) or in the wallbox (DC route, much more expensive box).

nerd_note.en: Renault 5 / Alpine A290 use the AC route with the Mobilize PowerBox Verso; VW ID. cars use the DC route (R-01; Volkswagen Austria, retrieved 2026-11-15). Eligibility for a used car is shown as conditions, never a plain tick, when software, battery size or build date matter (bidi spec §3).

short.en: Run a kettle, tools or camping gear from the car through a socket or an adapter.
short.nl: Gebruik een waterkoker, gereedschap of kampeerspullen via een stopcontact of adapter in de auto.

long.en: With V2L the car gives out household power through a socket in the car or an adapter in the charging port. It is quite common on newer cars and needs no installation. It is not the same as powering your house: a car with a socket for appliances cannot run your home just because of that.

nerd_note.en: The maximum power out differs by car and is stored per car as max_kw_out with its source; we show 'not disclosed' where the maker gives no figure.

label.nl: Kan je huis van stroom voorzien

short.en: The car's battery runs your home, for example in the evening or during a power cut.
short.nl: De accu van de auto voedt je huis, bijvoorbeeld 's avonds of bij een stroomstoring.

long.en: With V2H the car supplies your house through a special wallbox and installation. Whether it works depends on the car, its software version and battery size, the approved wallbox and your country. On a used car, check the conditions before you count on it.

nerd_note.en: Example of conditions: Volkswagen says ID. cars with Software 6 can charge both ways, while Software 3.5 cars need a battery of 77 kWh or more and are capped at 10,000 kWh or 4,000 hours of discharge (Volkswagen Austria, retrieved 2026-11-15).

label.en: Can earn by feeding the grid
label.nl: Kan verdienen door terug te leveren

short.en: The car sends power back to the grid when it is needed. Needs a matching wallbox and energy contract.
short.nl: De auto levert stroom terug aan het net als dat nodig is. Vraagt een passende wallbox en contract.

long.en: With V2G the car charges when power is cheap and sends some back when the grid needs it, and an energy company pays or credits you for it. It needs an approved wallbox and an energy contract that supports it. In 2026 it is live in only a few countries, for specific cars, wallboxes and contracts.

nerd_note.en: First commercial offer: Renault 5 / Alpine A290 with the PowerBox Verso and a Mobilize Power contract in France, October 2024 (electrive, 2024-10-22). Germany stopped double grid fees and electricity tax on stored power fed back in November 2025 (electrive, 2025-11-14).

label.nl: Kan een gebouw van stroom voorzien

short.en: Like powering a home, but for an office or other building, often with several cars.
short.nl: Zoals een huis voeden, maar dan voor een kantoor of ander gebouw, vaak met meerdere auto's.

long.en: V2B works like V2H but supplies a larger building, such as an office or a depot. It is mostly a business setup with several cars and a building energy system. For private buyers V2H and V2G matter more.

nerd_note.en: Kept as its own mode in bidi_modes so business offers can be rows, not code (bidi spec §3.1).

short.en: How car and charger talk. Required on new EU wallboxes from 2027; it does not make them two-way.
short.nl: Hoe auto en laadpaal praten. Verplicht op nieuwe EU-wallboxen vanaf 2027; maakt ze niet tweerichting.

long.en: ISO 15118-20 is the language a car and a charger use to talk to each other. From 1 January 2027 every newly installed or renovated charging point in the EU must support it, including home and workplace wallboxes. It makes two-way charging possible on the software side, but the rules do not require two-way hardware, and the car must support the standard too.

nerd_note.en: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2025/656 amending AFIR (EUR-Lex; go-e and KEBA, retrieved 2026-11-15). Existing wallboxes need no replacement; Mode 2 portable chargers are not covered. Many cars sold up to about 2025 speak DIN 70121 / ISO 15118-2 instead (R-01).

label.en: Plug in and charge, no card

short.en: The charger recognises the car through the cable and bills your contract. No card or app needed.
short.nl: De laadpaal herkent de auto via de kabel en rekent af via je contract. Geen pas of app nodig.

long.en: With Plug & Charge the car identifies itself to the charger when you plug in, and the session is billed to your charging contract. The EU rules do not make it compulsory. Whether it works depends on the car, the charger network and your contract.

nerd_note.en: Public points with automatic authentication installed or renovated from 2027 must support both ISO 15118-2 and ISO 15118-20 (R-01, Delegated Regulation (EU) 2025/656 Annex 2.1.2).

short.en: The standard plug for home wallboxes and street posts in Europe and the UK. Every current car has it.
short.nl: De standaardstekker voor wallboxen en laadpalen in Europa en het VK. Elke huidige auto heeft hem.

long.en: Type 2 is the plug for slower AC charging at home, at work and at street posts. Every electric car sold new in Europe today has a Type 2 inlet. At many street posts you bring your own Type 2 cable.

nerd_note.en: Pre-2019 Tesla Model S and X used a modified Type 2 plug at Superchargers; Teslas sold in Europe now use CCS2 (R-01 §5). Connector row: connector_types `type2`.

short.en: The fast-charge plug on every new EV in Europe. The cable is fixed to the charger.
short.nl: De snellaadstekker op elke nieuwe EV in Europa. De kabel zit vast aan de lader.

long.en: CCS2 is the standard plug for DC fast charging in Europe and the UK. The car's socket combines the Type 2 shape with two extra pins for fast charging, so one inlet takes both plugs. At fast chargers the cable is attached to the charger, so you don't need your own.

nerd_note.en: Europe, the UK, Australia and New Zealand use CCS2 + Type 2; Tesla Europe moved to CCS2 (R-01 §5). Connector row: connector_types `ccs2`.

short.en: An older Japanese fast-charge plug on some used cars. CHAdeMO chargers are getting harder to find.
short.nl: Een oudere Japanse snellaadstekker op sommige occasions. CHAdeMO-laders worden steeds zeldzamer.

long.en: CHAdeMO is an older fast-charging plug found on some used cars, such as the first two generations of the Nissan Leaf, the Nissan e-NV200 and the Mitsubishi Outlander plug-in hybrid. Fewer new chargers support it. Before buying, check that there are enough working CHAdeMO chargers on the routes you drive.

nerd_note.en: CHAdeMO cars were the first route to V2G in Europe (for example Octopus's UK V2G tariff for legacy CHAdeMO cars), but compatible boxes are scarce (R-01; bidi caveat `chademo-legacy`).

short.en: EU law for public chargers: card payment at fast chargers, clear prices and chargers along main roads.
short.nl: EU-wet voor openbare laders: pinnen bij snelladers, duidelijke prijzen en laders langs hoofdwegen.

long.en: AFIR is the EU regulation for alternative fuels infrastructure, including public EV chargers. It requires bank-card payment at new fast chargers, prices shown before you start, and a minimum number of fast chargers along main European roads. It applies in every EU country, not in the UK, which has its own rules.

nerd_note.en: Applies since 13 April 2024. New public points of 50 kW+ must take bank cards; from 1 January 2027 existing 50 kW+ points on the TEN-T network too (Plugchoice). TEN-T core: a site every 60 km with 400 kW and one 150 kW point by end 2025, 600 kW and two by end 2027 (Nationale Leitstelle).

short.en: Charge and pay on the spot with a bank card, phone or QR code. No app or subscription needed.
short.nl: Ter plekke laden en betalen met pinpas, telefoon of QR-code. Geen app of abonnement nodig.

long.en: Ad-hoc payment means you can charge without signing up for anything. In the EU, new fast chargers must accept a bank card, while slower posts may use a QR code and a web page instead. A charger where you can only pay in cash does not meet the rules.

nerd_note.en: EU (AFIR): new public points of 50 kW+ built since 13 April 2024 need a card or contactless reader; below 50 kW QR/web payment is enough (Plugchoice). UK: contactless on all public points of 50 kW+ and on new points of 8 kW+ installed after 24 November 2024 (GreenFleet). Cash-only fails AFIR (EC Q&A Q5.7).

label.en: One app or card for many networks
label.nl: Eén app of pas voor veel netwerken

short.en: A charging app or card that works across many networks, so you don't need one per operator.
short.nl: Een laadapp of -pas die bij veel netwerken werkt, zodat je er niet één per aanbieder nodig hebt.

long.en: A roaming app or card lets you charge at many networks with one account. It is optional now that fast chargers take bank cards, but it can help where a charger has no card reader and is sometimes cheaper. Prices differ by app or card, so compare before you choose.

nerd_note.en: UK operators must let you pay through at least one roaming provider (GOV.UK, Public Charge Point Regulations 2023). Chargeprice compares session prices per card or app.

short.en: An extra charge per minute if your car stays plugged in after charging. Move the car when done.
short.nl: Extra kosten per minuut als je auto na het laden aangesloten blijft. Zet de auto weg als hij klaar is.

long.en: Some operators charge per minute when a car stays connected after it has finished charging, so the charger is free for the next driver. In the EU it may come on top of the price per kWh at fast chargers. The charger or app shows it before you start.

nerd_note.en: AFIR: at 50 kW+ the ad-hoc price is per kWh, with a per-minute fee for occupancy allowed on top (EC Q&A Q5.17 and Q5.19; Plugchoice).

short.en: The EU's main road network. Fast chargers must be placed at set distances along it.
short.nl: Het belangrijkste wegennet van de EU. Snelladers moeten er op vaste afstanden langs staan.

long.en: TEN-T is the EU's list of main transport routes, with a core network of the busiest corridors. The EU charging rules set a minimum charging offer along these roads. So on main motorways a fast charger is never far away, though there are still gaps.

nerd_note.en: Core network: a site at least every 60 km with 400 kW in total and one 150 kW+ point by end 2025, 600 kW and two 150 kW+ points by end 2027 (Nationale Leitstelle). 79 % of the core met the 2025 rule in June 2026 (T&E via electrive, 2026-07-20).

short.en: One place where one car can charge at a time. A charger can have several.
short.nl: Eén plek waar één auto tegelijk kan laden. Een laadpaal kan er meerdere hebben.

long.en: Countries count chargers in different ways, so we separate points, devices, locations and connectors. A point is where one car charges at a time; a device can hold several points, and a point can have several connectors. That is why charger counts from different countries should not be compared side by side.

nerd_note.en: We count points (EVSE) wherever the source allows, as AFIR, the UK DfT (since 2026) and EAFO do; each series keeps one definition_id (charging_definitions).

short.en: How much energy the battery can actually use, in kWh. Bigger usually means more range.
short.nl: Hoeveel energie de accu echt kan gebruiken, in kWh. Groter betekent meestal meer bereik.

long.en: Battery size is the energy the car can store and use, in kilowatt-hours. We show the usable (net) figure, because that is what you drive on. Makers often advertise the larger gross figure, so compare usable with usable.

nerd_note.en: Stored as battery_kwh_net. Where only gross is known, the value is labelled; see 'usable vs gross'.

short.en: What sellers typically ask for this car used in your country: the middle half of asking prices.
short.nl: Wat verkopers in jouw land meestal vragen voor deze auto als occasion: de middelste helft van de vraagprijzen.

long.en: The used price is a band of asking prices, not a valuation and not a final sale price. It shows the middle half of prices we see for this generation, by age and mileage, with the number of listings. With too few listings we show "not enough data" instead of a guess.

nerd_note.en: p25–p75 of asking prices per generation × country × age band × mileage band; hidden below 8 listings (spec §8). Until a listing source covers a country, a 'See listings' link replaces the band.

short.en: How many kilometres a fast charger adds in 10 minutes of motorway driving. Higher means shorter stops.
short.nl: Hoeveel kilometer snelweg een snellader in 10 minuten toevoegt. Hoger betekent kortere stops.

long.en: This is the short-stop version of our fast-charging figure. It combines the car's average charging speed with its motorway energy use, so it says how far a quick stop gets you. It assumes a suitable charger and a warm battery.

nerd_note.en: dc_km_per_10min = dc_avg_10_80_kw / motorway consumption (kWh/100 km) × 100 / 6 (schema PublishedVariant). Rankings use the 20-minute figure (Decision 009).

short.en: How strong the electric motor or motors are, in kilowatts. More power means quicker acceleration.
short.nl: Hoe sterk de elektromotor of -motoren zijn, in kilowatt. Meer vermogen betekent sneller optrekken.

long.en: Power is the most the motors can deliver, in kilowatts. It matters for overtaking and towing, but even modest electric cars feel quick from a standstill. Higher power does not always mean higher energy use.

nerd_note.en: Usually the maker's peak (system) figure; registration documents may list a lower continuous rating. The source of each figure is shown on hover.

short.en: Seconds from standstill to 100 km/h. Lower is quicker.
short.nl: Seconden van stilstand tot 100 km/u. Lager is sneller.

long.en: This is the time the car needs to reach 100 km/h from a standstill, as stated by the maker or a test. It is a rough guide to how lively the car feels. Battery charge and temperature can make real times a little slower.

nerd_note.en: Maker claims are marked as claims; test figures carry their own source and date.

short.en: Which wheels the motors drive: front, rear or all four.
short.nl: Welke wielen de motoren aandrijven: voor, achter of alle vier.

long.en: Front- or rear-wheel drive cars have one motor; all-wheel drive usually means a motor on each axle. All-wheel drive helps on snow and when towing, and often adds power. It usually uses a little more energy, so range can be slightly lower.

nerd_note.en: Drivetrain is a variant field; the trip check's 'snow / mountain roads' extra weighs AWD (trip-fit §4).

short.en: How heavy the car is, in kilograms. Heavier cars usually use a bit more energy.
short.nl: Hoe zwaar de auto is, in kilogram. Zwaardere auto's verbruiken meestal iets meer.

long.en: Weight is the mass of the car, mostly set by its size and battery. Sources differ on whether a driver and luggage are included, so small differences between cars mean little. Weight also matters for some driving licences and for towing limits.

nerd_note.en: Stored as weight_kg with the source's own definition in provenance; compare within one source where you can.

short.en: How many people the car is approved to carry, driver included.
short.nl: Hoeveel mensen de auto mag vervoeren, bestuurder meegerekend.

long.en: The number of seats the car is approved for, including the driver. Some models offer extra seats as an option, so check the exact car. A third row is often only suitable for children.

nerd_note.en: Per variant; optional seat rows are listed separately when a source gives them.

short.en: We worked this out from other sourced numbers, with the method shown, rather than copying it.
short.nl: Dit hebben we berekend uit andere bronnen, met de methode erbij, in plaats van het over te nemen.

long.en: Many of our headline numbers, such as real-world range and range added while charging, are calculated from other figures. Each one keeps the inputs and the method it came from. We compute our own figures instead of copying another site's tables.

nerd_note.en: Data rule 2, 'derived, not copied' (AGENTS.md). Provenance lists the input facts and the method or rung.

short.en: Our data is published in numbered releases with a date, so you know how fresh a number is.
short.nl: Onze data verschijnt in genummerde releases met een datum, zodat je weet hoe vers een getal is.

long.en: The catalogue is published in numbered releases. Each release replaces the previous one in one go and can be rolled back if something is wrong. The open data downloads carry the same release number and date.

nerd_note.en: Releases swap in atomically and can be rolled back (spec §12); each release has QA checks in qa.json (provenance and licence gates block).

short.en: Choose how much you see: key numbers in plain words, full specs, or raw values with sources.
short.nl: Kies hoeveel je ziet: kerncijfers in gewone woorden, alle specificaties, of ruwe waarden met bronnen.

long.en: Simple shows the headline numbers and a few filters. Detailed adds all filters and full spec tables. Nerd shows raw values and units, every source with its date and confidence, and the method behind each estimate.

nerd_note.en: Remembered per visitor and kept in the URL, so a shared link keeps the level (spec §4).

short.en: Whether this car does your regular trips in winter without charging: yes, tight or needs a stop.
short.nl: Of deze auto je vaste ritten in de winter haalt zonder te laden: ja, krap of een stop nodig.

long.en: You tell us your longest regular round trip, how much is motorway and where you live. We estimate the car's winter range on that mix and compare it with what you need. Cars that fall short stay visible, with the reason.

nerd_note.en: Energy needed = Σ road bands (km × consumption at speed and temperature) + warm-up + climb; energy available = usable kWh × battery health × (start charge − arrival buffer) (trip-fit §5). Tonight's matrix is a provisional fixture.

label.nl: Het bereik dat je echt nodig hebt

technical.en: Winter range need on your road mix

short.en: The winter range your longest regular trip takes, with a safety buffer, on your mix of roads.
short.nl: Het winterbereik dat je langste vaste rit vraagt, met een veiligheidsmarge, op jouw mix van wegen.

long.en: This is the range your biggest must-do trip needs in winter, plus a buffer. We show it in kilometres on your road mix and as a rough official-range equivalent, so you can compare it with adverts. Weather, tyres, speed and load change real results.

nerd_note.en: Shown with a P10–P90 band in Nerd mode; WLTP-equivalent uses the median WLTP ratio for that mix (trip-fit §5).

short.en: How much battery is left over after your trip. Too little, and the result is marked tight.
short.nl: Hoeveel accu er na je rit overblijft. Te weinig, en de uitkomst is krap.

long.en: The margin is the energy left after your trip, as a share of the usable battery. A clear margin gives a tick, a small one is marked tight, and a shortfall means you need a charging stop. It is an estimate, so a tight result deserves a closer look.

nerd_note.en: Verdict: ✓ margin ≥ 15 % of usable; ⚠ 0–15 % or the P10–P90 band crosses zero; ✗ short (trip-fit §5).

short.en: Town, rural roads or motorway. Each uses a different amount of energy per kilometre.
short.nl: Stad, buitenweg of snelweg. Elk verbruikt een andere hoeveelheid energie per kilometer.

long.en: We split a trip into town, rural and motorway driving, because speed changes energy use a lot. Motorway driving uses the most energy per kilometre, while town trips lose more to heating in winter. Your mix of road types decides your real range.

nerd_note.en: Bands: town ≤ 50 km/h roads, rural 60–90, motorway 100+; speed per band from a country speed profile ± driving style (trip-fit §5).

short.en: The spread in which the real result will most likely fall. A wider band means less certainty.
short.nl: De spreiding waarbinnen de echte uitkomst waarschijnlijk valt. Een bredere band betekent minder zekerheid.

long.en: Every estimate has some uncertainty, so we show a low and a high value next to the main one. In most cases the real figure falls between them. The band is wider when our method for that car is less precise.

nerd_note.en: P10–P90 from the confidence of the rung used (trip-fit §5). Simple mode shows only the verdict and one number.

short.en: How full the battery is when you leave. Daily trips assume your normal charging limit.
short.nl: Hoe vol de accu is als je vertrekt. Dagelijkse ritten gaan uit van je normale laadlimiet.

long.en: The trip check assumes you leave with the battery at your daily charging limit. For most batteries that is about 80 %, and 100 % for types that are fine to charge full every day. Rare long trips assume a full battery.

nerd_note.en: Weekly / monthly trips start at 80 % for NMC and 100 % where charge_100_daily is true; occasional and must-reach trips at 100 %; arrival buffer default 10 % (trip-fit §3, §5).

short.en: The usual temperature for that month in your area, from long-term weather records.
short.nl: De gebruikelijke temperatuur voor die maand in jouw omgeving, uit langjarige weergegevens.

long.en: We check trips on a normal January day near you, not on the coldest day ever recorded. The temperature comes from long-term averages for your town. You can also check a colder day for snow or mountain trips.

nerd_note.en: Planned source: Meteostat climate normals (licence to confirm), fallback Copernicus ERA5 monthly means (trip-fit §7). Tonight's town list is a fixture.

short.en: The official (WLTP) range a car would need to cover your trip, to compare with adverts.
short.nl: De officiële (WLTP-)actieradius die een auto nodig heeft voor je rit, om met advertenties te vergelijken.

long.en: Adverts quote the official WLTP range, which is higher than what you get in winter. We convert the range you need into the WLTP figure a typical car would need. It is a rough guide for reading adverts, not a promise.

nerd_note.en: Uses the median WLTP ratio for your road mix and season (trip-fit §5).

short.en: Show prices as a cash price, a monthly loan estimate or a monthly lease.
short.nl: Toon prijzen als koopprijs, maandschatting voor een lening of maandbedrag voor lease.

long.en: Many buyers don't pay cash, so every price can switch between buying outright, a loan per month and a lease per month. Loan figures are our own estimate, not an offer. The choice is remembered and kept in the link.

nerd_note.en: Lease shows labelled links only until partner feeds exist; no UK finance or lease links until FCA credit-broking rules are checked (spec §8).

short.en: The yearly cost of a loan, including most fees, as a percentage. Lower is cheaper.
short.nl: De jaarlijkse kosten van een lening, inclusief de meeste kosten, als percentage. Lager is goedkoper.

long.en: The APR shows the total cost of borrowing as a yearly percentage, so loans can be compared. Our calculator uses a typical national rate where an official statistic exists, or asks you to enter one. Your own rate depends on the lender and your situation.

nerd_note.en: EU consumer credit directive CCD2 (Directive (EU) 2023/2225) applies from 20 November 2026 (spec §8). Typical rates and their sources live in finance_profiles; with no source the field stays empty.

short.en: The part of the price you pay yourself at the start. The rest is borrowed.
short.nl: Het deel van de prijs dat je zelf aan het begin betaalt. De rest leen je.

long.en: A deposit is the money you put down when you buy. A bigger deposit means borrowing less, so the monthly amount and the total interest go down. You can change it in the calculator.

nerd_note.en: Default deposit per country comes from finance_profiles only where a source states one; otherwise the calculator asks.

short.en: How many months you pay. Longer means lower monthly amounts but more interest in total.
short.nl: Hoeveel maanden je betaalt. Langer betekent lagere maandbedragen maar meer rente in totaal.

long.en: The term is how long you take to repay a loan or how long a lease runs. Spreading payments over more months lowers each payment but raises the total you pay. Our calculator starts at 48 months, and you can change it.

nerd_note.en: Default 48 months (spec §8 'Ways to pay'); finance_profiles may set a country default when a source states one.

technical.en: Common APK defects by first-registration year

short.en: The defects Dutch inspectors find most often on this generation, compared with other EVs of the same age.
short.nl: De gebreken die Nederlandse keurmeesters het vaakst vinden bij deze generatie, vergeleken met andere EV's van dezelfde leeftijd.

long.en: This block counts the defects found at the Dutch periodic inspection (APK) for this generation, from RDW open data. Cars are grouped by the year they were first registered, and each rate is compared with all sampled EVs from that same year, never with older or younger cars. A high rate is a hint for what to check before you buy, not proof that a car is unreliable.

nerd_note.en: RDW inspections and defects datasets (CC0), light-vehicle APK only, on a fixed ~10 % plate sample of EVs first registered from 2010. A year needs at least 20 sampled cars and a defect at least 3 cars; the top 5 defects per year are kept. The defects seen so far are wear items such as tyres, lights, wheel bearings and ball joints.

short.en: The Netherlands' required periodic roadworthiness test for cars, like the UK MOT. RDW publishes the defects found.
short.nl: De verplichte periodieke keuring van je auto. De RDW publiceert welke gebreken keurmeesters vinden.

long.en: The APK is the periodic roadworthiness inspection that cars in the Netherlands must pass to stay on the road. Inspectors record every defect they find, and RDW publishes those records as open data per number plate. That makes it one of the few open sources that shows how a model holds up with age. The data lists defects only: it has no pass or fail result and no odometer reading.

nerd_note.en: RDW datasets Keuringen (vkij-7mwc), Geconstateerde Gebreken (a34c-vvps) and the defect code list Gebreken (hx2c-gt7k), all CC0. UK equivalent: the MOT, due by a car's third registration anniversary and then yearly (gov.uk/getting-an-mot); DVSA publishes MOT results as open data (OGL).

short.en: The range from the official US test. It is usually lower than the European WLTP figure for the same car.
short.nl: Het bereik uit de officiële Amerikaanse test. Meestal lager dan het Europese WLTP-cijfer voor dezelfde auto.

long.en: The US Environmental Protection Agency rates cars sold in the US with its own five-cycle test. Its range figure is usually lower than the WLTP figure for the same car. We show it as a separate number and never mix it with WLTP. It only exists for cars sold in the US, and US versions can differ from European ones, for example in charger options.

nerd_note.en: From fueleconomy.gov (US public domain), with OpenEV as fallback; merged only with other EPA figures (2 % tolerance) and converted from miles to km. When several US trims or model years map to one variant, the earliest model year of the primary source wins and the rest go to the conflicts list, never averaged.

short.en: The year the car was first registered, from the Dutch register. Inspection results are only compared within one year.
short.nl: Het jaar waarin de auto voor het eerst op kenteken kwam. Keuringsresultaten vergelijken we alleen binnen hetzelfde jaar.

long.en: This is the year a car was first registered, taken from the first-admission date in the RDW register. Cars from the same year have had the same time to age, so we group inspection results by this year and compare each generation only with other EVs registered in that year. It is close to the car's age, but it is not the same as its model year.

nerd_note.en: RDW field datum_eerste_toelating. A separate field, datum_eerste_tenaamstelling_in_nederland, holds the first Dutch registration, which can be later for imported cars. Age = fetch year minus this year.

short.en: Of every 100 sampled cars of this generation and year, how many had this defect noted at the APK.
short.nl: Van elke 100 auto's in de steekproef van deze generatie en dit jaar: hoeveel dit gebrek hadden bij de APK.

long.en: The rate counts cars, not defect reports, for one generation and one first-registration year. Cars with no APK report in the period count as zero, so the base is every sampled car, not only the inspected ones. Each rate sits next to the same figure for all sampled EVs first registered in that year. Years with few reports are hidden by default, because a handful of cars can swing the number a lot.

nerd_note.en: Rate = cars with the defect ÷ sampled cars × 100. Years with fewer than 20 sampled cars are left out; years with few reports (under 10 % of cars, or under 10 cars, with a report) are hidden by default. 'About as often' means within 20 % of the same-year baseline (or 1 per 100): a display rule, not a statistical test.

short.en: Charging points grouped by maximum power, from slow AC to ultra-fast DC of 350 kW and more.
short.nl: Laadpunten gegroepeerd naar maximaal vermogen, van langzaam AC tot ultrasnel DC van 350 kW en meer.

long.en: Official statistics group public charging points by how much power they can deliver. We map each source's own bands onto five of ours: AC under 22 kW, AC 22 kW, DC 50–149 kW, DC 150–349 kW and DC 350 kW and more. Sources draw their lines differently, so a chart only shows the bands a source really reports.

nerd_note.en: Source bands (EAFO, BNetzA and others) keep their own ids and map onto ours. One chart uses one source definition, never a mix (Decision 012).

short.en: We compare our generation start and end years with Wikidata. A mismatch is flagged, never silently changed.
short.nl: We vergelijken onze begin- en eindjaren met Wikidata. Een verschil wordt gemeld, nooit stilletjes aangepast.

long.en: Wikidata is an open (CC0) knowledge base that records, among other things, when car models were introduced and ended. We check each generation's start and end years against it. When every Wikidata year falls within one year of ours, the badge says the years are checked; when one does not, it says Wikidata disagrees and Nerd mode shows the details. Wikidata never changes our years: a disagreement is flagged for review.

nerd_note.en: Corroborated = every Wikidata year within ±1 of the nearest seed boundary of the same kind (start or end). Wikidata is model-level and sparse, so we use it for names and years only (R-08). Known disagreements so far: a concept-car year and a China-only item.

short.en: Run a kettle, tools or a camping fridge from the car through a socket or adapter.
short.nl: Gebruik een waterkoker, gereedschap of koelbox via een stopcontact of adapter in de auto.

explainer.en: The car gives out household power through a socket or a plug-in adapter, usually about 2 to 3.6 kW. It is common on newer cars. V2L is not the same as powering your home: that needs V2H and a special installation.
explainer.nl: De auto levert stroom via een stopcontact of adapter, meestal 2 tot 3,6 kW. V2L is niet hetzelfde als je huis van stroom voorzien; daarvoor is V2H nodig.

label.nl: Kan je huis van stroom voorzien

short.en: The car's battery runs your home, for example in the evening or during a power cut.
short.nl: De accu van de auto voedt je huis, bijvoorbeeld 's avonds of bij een stroomstoring.

explainer.en: With an approved wallbox the car can supply your home. Whether it works depends on the car, its software version and battery size, the wallbox and your country.
explainer.nl: Met een goedgekeurde wallbox kan de auto je huis voeden. Of het werkt hangt af van de auto, de softwareversie, de accugrootte, de wallbox en je land.

label.en: Can earn by feeding the grid
label.nl: Kan verdienen door terug te leveren

short.en: The car sells power back to the grid at busy times. Needs a matching box and energy contract.
short.nl: De auto levert stroom terug aan het net op drukke momenten. Vraagt een passende box en contract.

explainer.en: The car charges when power is cheap and feeds some back when it is in demand, and an energy company pays or credits you for it. In 2026 this is live in a few countries only, for specific cars, wallboxes and contracts.
explainer.nl: De auto laadt als stroom goedkoop is en levert terug als er vraag is; een energiebedrijf vergoedt dat. In 2026 kan dit pas in een paar landen, met specifieke auto's, boxen en contracten.

label.nl: Kan een gebouw van stroom voorzien

short.en: Like powering a home, but for an office or other building, often with several cars.
short.nl: Zoals een huis voeden, maar dan voor een kantoor of ander gebouw, vaak met meerdere auto's.

short.en: The car converts the power itself, so a matching wallbox costs about as much as a normal one.
short.nl: De auto zet de stroom zelf om, dus een passende wallbox kost ongeveer zoveel als een gewone.

explainer.en: The inverter sits in the car's on-board charger. You still need a wallbox the maker approves, but it is priced close to a normal wallbox. Examples: Renault 5 and 4, Alpine A290, BMW iX3 (Neue Klasse), Nissan Leaf third generation.
explainer.nl: De omvormer zit in de lader van de auto. Je hebt nog wel een goedgekeurde wallbox nodig, maar die kost ongeveer zoveel als een gewone.

short.en: The wallbox converts the power, so it costs more, roughly €2,000–3,000 or above.
short.nl: De wallbox zet de stroom om en is daardoor duurder, grofweg €2.000–3.000 of meer.

explainer.en: The inverter sits in the wallbox, which makes the box much dearer than a normal one. Examples: Volkswagen group cars on MEB with a large battery and recent software, Mercedes GLC and C-Class EQ, Ford Explorer and Capri.
explainer.nl: De omvormer zit in de wallbox, waardoor die veel duurder is dan een gewone. Voorbeelden: VW-groep op MEB met grote accu en recente software, Mercedes GLC en C-Klasse EQ.

short.en: Older cars with a CHAdeMO plug, like early Nissan Leafs. Matching boxes are getting scarce.
short.nl: Oudere auto's met CHAdeMO-stekker, zoals vroege Nissan Leafs. Passende boxen worden schaars.

short.en: Works only with the maker's own equipment. Check what is needed before you buy.
short.nl: Werkt alleen met apparatuur van het merk zelf. Kijk vóór aankoop wat nodig is.

short.en: The language new EU chargers must speak from 2027. It allows two-way charging but doesn't guarantee it.
short.nl: De taal die nieuwe EU-laders vanaf 2027 moeten spreken. Maakt terugleveren mogelijk, niet zeker.

explainer.en: From 1 January 2027 every newly installed or renovated EU charging point, home wallboxes included, must speak ISO 15118-20. That makes a wallbox ready on the software side, but most will still not be able to send power back. The car must speak it too, and makers rarely say.
explainer.nl: Vanaf 1 januari 2027 moet elk nieuw of vernieuwd EU-laadpunt, ook thuis, ISO 15118-20 spreken. Dat maakt de wallbox softwarematig klaar, maar de meeste kunnen nog steeds geen stroom terugleveren.

label.nl: Oudere standaard met uitbreiding van het merk

technical.nl: ISO 15118-2 met uitbreiding van het merk

short.en: Two-way charging built on the older ISO 15118-2 standard, as in Volkswagen's current system.
short.nl: Terugleveren op basis van de oudere ISO 15118-2, zoals in het huidige systeem van Volkswagen.

short.en: The Japanese fast-charge standard that did two-way charging first. Mostly older cars in Europe.
short.nl: De Japanse snellaadstandaard die als eerste terugleverde. In Europa vooral oudere auto's.

short.en: A maker-specific way of talking to the box. Works only with approved equipment.
short.nl: Een merkeigen manier van communiceren met de box. Werkt alleen met goedgekeurde apparatuur.

technical.en: Protocol not disclosed by the maker
technical.nl: Protocol niet bekendgemaakt door het merk

short.en: The maker doesn't say which protocol the car uses. We never guess it from the model year.
short.nl: Het merk zegt niet welk protocol de auto gebruikt. We gokken het nooit op basis van bouwjaar.

short.en: The car can only send power back through an expensive DC wallbox.
short.nl: De auto kan alleen terugleveren via een dure DC-wallbox.

label.nl: Alleen met de wallbox van het merk

short.en: Other wallboxes won't work for two-way charging, even bidirectional ones.
short.nl: Andere wallboxen werken niet voor terugleveren, ook niet als ze bidirectioneel zijn.

short.en: Feeding the grid only works with a matching contract from a named energy company.
short.nl: Terugleveren werkt alleen met een passend contract van een bepaald energiebedrijf.

label.en: Needs software {param} or newer — check the car
label.nl: Vraagt software {param} of nieuwer — controleer de auto

short.en: Ask the seller which software version the car runs. Older versions can't do it.
short.nl: Vraag de verkoper welke softwareversie de auto heeft. Oudere versies kunnen het niet.

label.en: Large battery only ({param} kWh or more)
label.nl: Alleen grote accu ({param} kWh of meer)

short.en: Smaller-battery versions of this car are excluded. Check the usable battery size.
short.nl: Versies met een kleinere accu vallen af. Controleer de bruikbare accucapaciteit.

short.en: Older cars of the same model can't do it. Check the build date, not just the year.
short.nl: Oudere auto's van hetzelfde model kunnen het niet. Kijk naar de bouwdatum, niet alleen het jaar.

short.en: The maker caps how much energy you may send back without affecting the battery warranty.
short.nl: Het merk begrenst hoeveel energie je mag terugleveren zonder gevolgen voor de accugarantie.

label.en: Old CHAdeMO plug — boxes getting scarce

short.en: Two-way boxes for this plug are hard to find new. Check before you count on it.
